title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
This is an operational envelope failure rather than a perception or prediction error. The vehicles performed as designed in ordinary traffic, then ran out of charge when congestion turned a normal trip into a prolonged standstill, and the fleet had no way to complete the trips it had accepted. The failure surfaced at the level of fleet energy management and dispatch, not in the driving task itself. A separate vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks left in the road, which is an environmental hazard rather than a failure of the driving system.

Catching this would have required treating extended gridlock as a foreseeable condition rather than an anomaly. That means monitoring remaining charge against time spent stationary, not only against distance, and holding or rerouting vehicles once a standstill exceeds what their batteries can absorb. The company's own account points to traffic volume and unexpected road closures, both of which are visible to a dispatch system before a vehicle is committed to a route. The December incident at non-functioning traffic lights suggests the same class of gap, a fleet that continues operating when the conditions around it have changed.

What is not established is the underlying cause of the battery drain beyond the company's stated explanation, which is a statement by an interested party and not an independent finding. No regulatory determination has been reported, and no injuries were reported. The single outlet account does not establish how many vehicles were affected beyond the dozen visible in footage, or whether any person was harmed or cited.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets on July 5th after their batteries drained during severe traffic congestion following Fourth of July fireworks celebrations. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on city streets, with some requiring towing. The company attributed the problem to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unexpected road closures. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks on the street, though no injuries were reported. Frustrated motorists spent hours in standstill traffic, with some angry at the stranded autonomous vehicles blocking roadways.

Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles, and the company stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic disruptions. Mayor Daniel Lurie urged residents to be patient as streets cleared. City officials announced plans to discuss the incident with public and private partners to prevent similar problems during future events. This incident echoes a December incident when a power outage caused some Waymo vehicles to stall at non-functioning traffic lights.
